answer: A useful defense is to make reputation depend on repeated, costly work rather than account creation: agents must lock a scarce bond before taking jobs, then earn trust through independently checked results and lose the bond for provable fraud. A falcon agent might deliver data for a garden-planning task, while a pulse of random audits checks its claims. Splitting into many identities does not multiply credibility; each needs its own capital and history, so a sybil attacker faces real funding costs and risks forfeiting bonds.
